messages:
Matt H: Hey everyone, first day here. I installed the company WireGuard profile but I cant reach the dev bastion (10.20.5.2) or any 10.20.x services. Public sites are fine. Who do I bug for access?
Sarah I (eng-infra): Welcome Matt! Two quick checks: what IP did WG assign you and can you paste `ifconfig` (or `ip a`) and `traceroute 10.20.5.2`? Also try `dig @10.100.0.2 internal.service.redwood` to see if internal DNS was pushed.
Matt H: Assigned IP is 172.16.50.12. Traceroute output:
``
traceroute to 10.20.5.2 (10.20.5.2), 64 hops max, 52 byte packets
 1  172.16.50.1  1.12 ms  1.03 ms  0.98 ms
 2  * * *
```
`dig @10.100.0.2 internal.service.redwood` just times out. I'm on macOS Ventura (M1).
Jamie (sre): Likely split-tunnel didn't include 10.20.0.0/16 or DNS wasn't pushed. Can you run `sudo route -n get 10.20.5.2` and `scutil --dns` and paste results? Also check the WG comment header in the profile (infra often lists pushed routes).
Matt H: `sudo route -n get 10.20.5.2` shows:
``
route to: 10.20.5.2
destination: 10.20.5.2
interface: utun2
  type: UTUN
  gateway: 172.16.50.1
```
But `scutil --dns` has no 10.100.0.2 entry.
Sarah I (eng-infra): OK that matches missing DNS. Two options: infra can reissue the client profile to push DNS and the 10.20.0.0/16 route, or you can temporarily add a resolver file on mac to hit internal DNS. Try:
``
sudo mkdir -p /etc/resolver
echo 'nameserver 10.100.0.2' | sudo tee /etc/resolver/redwood
sudo dscacheutil -flushcache
```
Then test `dig internal.service.redwood @10.100.0.2`. If you get an A record (10.20.x.x) but still cant reach the host, it may be route-related.
Jamie (sre): If DNS returns an internal IP but traffic still drops after first hop, add a route temporarily: `sudo route -n add -net 10.20.0.0/16 172.16.50.1`. That should force the 10.20 network over the VPN utun gateway. Note mac route syntax expects the net/mask form.
Matt H: I added the resolver entry, `dig` now returns `10.20.12.8`. SSH `ubuntu@10.20.12.8` still timed out, so I applied the route add and now SSH connects.
sec-bot: Security alert: we noticed traffic from client 172.16.50.12 to prod-like CIDR. By default dev SGs allow only 172.16.50.0/24. If you need broader access open a short access request ticket to infra with manager approval.
Sarah I (eng-infra): Thanks Matt. Jamie, can you confirm well push DNS and the 10.20 route in the WG profile? Ill update the onboarding doc with the temporary resolver / route steps until the new profile is live.
Jamie (sre): Done. I updated the profile to include 10.20.0.0/16 and to push DNS 10.100.0.2, then invalidated existing sessions so clients must reconnect and pick the new settings. Infra-bot also sent a reissue notification.
Matt H: Reconnected and everything works now. Can SSH and hit internal dashboards. Thanks all! :tada:
Sarah I (eng-infra): Welcome aboard, Matt! If anything else pops up ping #eng-infra or @infra-bot. :wave:
